identity.bot_interaction_pattern: Inline + lazy cache. The bot calls `commitments.py record` inline when it judges (during normal turn handling) that the current operator turn contained a commitment — there is NO separate transcript-scan sweep. A daily 03:30 launchd cron runs `list-due` and writes overdue follow-ups to `memory/commitments/followups-cache.md`; the bot reads that cache ONCE at the start of a new conversation via an AGENTS.md instruction. The bot does NOT poll commitments on heartbeats — that was the regression this version fixes.

observable_outcomes: When the operator says 'I'll send X to Alice by Friday' in conversation, the bot records it inline during its reply — an entry appears under memory/contacts/alice.md's Commitments section before the bot finishes responding

quality_bar.minimum: Operator can say 'I'll do X for Y by Friday', then ask 'what do I owe Y?' and see the commitment surfaced. The next morning, the bot mentions any overdue commitments in the first reply of that day's conversation.
quality_bar.excellent: Detection precision is high enough that operators don't see false-positive commitments (e.g. 'I'll think about it' is not recorded). Overdue commitments surface naturally in the bot's first reply of each new conversation, drawn from the daily cache. mark-done is offered as a one-line bot suggestion when the operator confirms completion in conversation.

privacy: Commitment text often references specific people and obligations — entries live only in memory/contacts/{slug}.md (Contacts app) and the followups cache. Never in shared logs, never in audit emissions beyond the slug + first 80 chars of text in FOLLOWUP_DUE:
The followups cache mirrors `list-due` stdout (FOLLOWUP_DUE: lines only). Rotated each cron run, no history retained.
safety: All Contacts writes go through `contacts.py add-commitment` (the canonical CLI) — never write to memory/contacts/{slug}.md directly. This preserves the append-only invariant and slug normalization.
mark-done modifies an existing line via strikethrough — the script must preserve the original commitment text and date verbatim, only adding `~~ ~~` around the text portion
list-due is read-only with respect to Contacts — never mutate while iterating

dependencies: Contacts (p-4136a932) — REQUIRED. `scripts/contacts.py` must exist; commitments.py shells out to it for storage.
boundaries: Detection is the bot's job, not the script's — `record` accepts whatever the bot supplies; no NLP heuristics in Python
list-due cadence is owned by launchd (cron at 03:30 local). The CLI does not self-throttle; manual invocations during the day are always allowed.
Inline detection happens during normal turn handling, not via a separate scan sweep. No scan cursor file.

build_spec:
# Commitment Tracker — Build Specification

## Overview

A thin behavior layer on top of the Contacts app. Three CLI subcommands (`record`, `list-due`, `mark-done`, `status`), a daily 03:30 launchd cron that refreshes a follow-ups cache, and two AGENTS.md session-start instructions (one for inline detection, one for surfacing the cache).

The tracker does NOT own the commitment data format — Contacts does. The tracker exists to make commitment capture and surfacing routine without requiring the operator to memorize Contacts CLI syntax.

**Prerequisite:** Contacts (p-4136a932) must already be installed — `scripts/contacts.py` is the storage gateway.

**v2026.06.08-1.1 architecture change:** the two heartbeat instructions from v1.0 (transcript-scan + daily-followups) were retired after the 2026-06-08 incident — they billed per-heartbeat tokens even when there were no new turns to scan and nothing was due. Replaced with: (a) inline detection during normal turn handling (no separate sweep), and (b) a daily launchd cron + lazy-read cache for follow-ups.

## Python invocation

Use `python3` (let the deploy environment resolve the binary). Do not hardcode venv paths.

## File layout

```
scripts/
  commitments.py                              ← main CLI (record | list-due | mark-done | status)
  commitment-tracker-cache-cron.sh            ← launchd wrapper: runs list-due, writes the cache
memory/
  commitments/
    followups-cache.md                        ← daily-refreshed cache of FOLLOWUP_DUE: lines
```

No `scan-cursor.json` — inline detection means the bot processes each operator turn exactly once at arrival, so there is nothing to bookmark.

## scripts/commitments.py

### Subcommands

```
commitments.py record    --person NAME --text TEXT [--due YYYY-MM-DD]
commitments.py list-due
commitments.py mark-done --person NAME --text-contains SUBSTRING
commitments.py status
```

### record

Shell out to Contacts:

```python
import subprocess, sys
from pathlib import Path

def record(workspace: Path, person: str, text: str, due: str | None) -> int:
    contacts_cli = workspace / "scripts" / "contacts.py"
    if not contacts_cli.exists():
        print("ERROR: Contacts app not installed (scripts/contacts.py missing)", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    cmd = ["python3", str(contacts_cli), "add-commitment",
           "--person", person, "--text", text]
    if due:
        cmd += ["--due", due]
    result = subprocess.run(cmd, cwd=str(workspace), capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=10)
    sys.stdout.write(result.stdout)
    sys.stderr.write(result.stderr)
    return result.returncode
```

No deduplication at this layer — the Contacts file is append-only and the bot is expected to record each fresh commitment exactly once. Re-recording is harmless but produces a duplicate line; the scan cursor (below) is the dedup mechanism for heartbeat-driven scans.

### list-due

Shell out to Contacts and pass through:

```python
def list_due(workspace: Path) -> int:
    contacts_cli = workspace / "scripts" / "contacts.py"
    if not contacts_cli.exists():
        return 2
    result = subprocess.run(
        ["python3", str(contacts_cli), "list-due"],
        cwd=str(workspace), capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=10,
    )
    sys.stdout.write(result.stdout)
    sys.stderr.write(result.stderr)
    return result.returncode
```

**Contract:** output is byte-identical to `contacts.py list-due` — the same `FOLLOWUP_DUE: {slug} | {text}` lines. Downstream consumers like Evening Sweep parse one canonical format.

### mark-done

Locate the unique commitment line in the contact file and replace its text portion with `~~text~~`:

```python
def mark_done(workspace: Path, person: str, contains: str) -> int:
    slug = person.strip().lower().replace(" ", "-")
    contact_file = workspace / "memory" / "contacts" / f"{slug}.md"
    if not contact_file.exists():
        print(f"No contact file for {person}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    text = contact_file.read_text()
    lines = text.splitlines(keepends=True)
    matches = [i for i, ln in enumerate(lines)
               if ln.startswith("- ") and contains in ln and "~~" not in ln]
    if len(matches) == 0:
        print("No matching commitment line found", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    if len(matches) > 1:
        print(f"Ambiguous: {len(matches)} matching lines. Be more specific.", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    i = matches[0]
    # Replace the text portion between the date prefix and any [due:] suffix
    line = lines[i].rstrip("\n")
    # Format: '- YYYY-MM-DD: TEXT [due: YYYY-MM-DD]?'
    if ": " not in line:
        return 1
    prefix, rest = line.split(": ", 1)
    if " [due:" in rest:
        text_part, due_part = rest.split(" [due:", 1)
        due_part = " [due:" + due_part
    else:
        text_part, due_part = rest, ""
    lines[i] = f"{prefix}: ~~{text_part}~~{due_part}\n"
    # Atomic write
    import os, tempfile
    fd, tmp = tempfile.mkstemp(dir=contact_file.parent, suffix=".tmp")
    with os.fdopen(fd, "w") as f:
        f.writelines(lines)
    os.replace(tmp, contact_file)
    print(f"Marked done: {text_part.strip()}")
    return 0
```

If no match or ambiguous: exit non-zero with a hint, do not mutate. The bot is expected to retry with a longer `--text-contains` substring.

### status

Print a one-screen summary: count of contacts files with commitments, count of past-due, count of struck-through (done) lines, last scan cursor timestamp.

## Scheduled Behavior — launchd cron + session-start instructions

Three `scheduled_actions[]` entries are declared on this manifest (below). Phase 4.5 reads them and dispatches to `install_launchd_command_action` (for the cron) or `install_heartbeat_instruction` (for the AGENTS.md session_instructions). None of them use HEARTBEAT.md.

**Action 1 — `commitment-tracker-cache-followups`** (`mechanism: launchd`). Fires daily at 03:30 local via `StartCalendarInterval {Hour=3, Minute=30}`. Calls `scripts/commitment-tracker-cache-cron.sh` which runs `python3 scripts/commitments.py list-due > memory/commitments/followups-cache.md` (atomically via temp file + os.replace). If nothing is overdue, the file is zero bytes — that empty signal tells the session-greet instruction to stay silent.

**Action 2 — `commitment-tracker-session-greet`** (`mechanism: oc_session_instruction`). Installs a `## Commitment Tracker — Session Greet` section in AGENTS.md. On the first turn of an operator-initiated session, the bot reads `memory/commitments/followups-cache.md`; if non-empty, surfaces the FOLLOWUP_DUE: lines naturally in its first reply. If empty/missing, stays silent on commitments unless asked. Fires once per session, NOT per heartbeat.

**Action 3 — `commitment-tracker-detect-inline`** (`mechanism: oc_session_instruction`). Installs a `## Commitment Tracker — Detect Inline` section in AGENTS.md. Throughout the session, when an operator turn contains a genuine commitment phrase, the bot calls `python3 scripts/commitments.py record --person NAME --text TEXT [--due DATE]` inline as part of its normal reply. No separate transcript-scan sweep.

## scripts/commitment-tracker-cache-cron.sh

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# commitment-tracker-cache-cron.sh — launchd wrapper.
# Runs list-due and writes the output to memory/commitments/followups-cache.md
# atomically. Quiet on success; errors to /tmp.

WORKSPACE="/Users/{bot_id}/.openclaw/workspace"
CACHE="$WORKSPACE/memory/commitments/followups-cache.md"
LOGFILE="/tmp/{bot_id}-commitment-tracker-cache.log"

cd "$WORKSPACE" || exit 1
mkdir -p "$(dirname "$CACHE")"

TMP=$(mktemp "$(dirname "$CACHE")/.cache.XXXXXX")
if /usr/bin/python3 "$WORKSPACE/scripts/commitments.py" list-due > "$TMP" 2>> "$LOGFILE"; then
  mv "$TMP" "$CACHE"
else
  echo "$(date -u +%FT%TZ) list-due failed; previous cache preserved" >> "$LOGFILE"
  rm -f "$TMP"
fi

exit 0
```

Make it executable: `chmod +x scripts/commitment-tracker-cache-cron.sh`.

The launchd plist is rendered by Phase 4.5's `install_launchd_command_action` from `scheduled_actions[*].install` — do NOT author it in this script.

## Test surface

```bash
python3 -m py_compile scripts/commitments.py
python3 scripts/commitments.py status
# Expected: prints zero counts on a fresh install
python3 scripts/commitments.py record --person "Test Person" --text "Test commitment" --due 2099-01-01
# Expected: shells to contacts.py, returns 0. memory/contacts/test-person.md should now exist.
python3 scripts/commitments.py list-due
# Expected: no output (due date is in the future)
python3 scripts/commitments.py mark-done --person "Test Person" --text-contains "Test commitment"
# Expected: 'Marked done: Test commitment'. The line in memory/contacts/test-person.md should be struck through.
```

## Provenance marker

```python
# evolve: pkg=p-3b4f5d29 file=f-XXXXXXXX@<version>
```

## What NOT to include

- **No HEARTBEAT.md section for this app.** Heartbeat-driven polling of `list-due` or transcript sweeps burns tokens on every bot turn even when nothing is overdue and no new commitments are in flight — that was the 2026-06-08 regression this version fixes. If a future reviewer asks 'why not heartbeat?', the answer is the cron + session-greet + inline-detect trio gives the same coverage at a fraction of the cost.
- No NLP / regex commitment detection in Python — the bot's LLM is the detector, operating inline.
- No `memory/commitments/scan-cursor.json` (or any other scan bookmark). Inline detection means no re-scan, so no bookmark is needed.
- No direct writes to memory/contacts/{slug}.md (except the targeted strikethrough in mark-done) — all other writes go through contacts.py.
- No openclaw.json mutation (Phase 4.5 installs the launchd plist and the two AGENTS.md sections; that's all).
- No background daemons or sleep loops (launchd handles cadence).
- No `/tmp` log files written from the Python script (logs go to stdout/stderr; the cron wrapper redirects to `/tmp/{bot_id}-commitment-tracker-cache.log`).

install.body:
At the start of a fresh operator-initiated conversation, read `memory/commitments/followups-cache.md`. If the file exists and is non-empty, surface its `FOLLOWUP_DUE: {slug} | {text}` lines naturally as a short bulleted reminder in your first reply — name the person and the commitment text plainly. If the file is empty or absent, say nothing about commitments and stay silent on this topic for the rest of the session unless the operator asks.

Do NOT run `commitments.py list-due` on every heartbeat or every turn. A daily launchd cron (`scripts/commitment-tracker-cache-cron.sh`) at 03:30 local refreshes this cache. Polling the CLI on heartbeats is a regression and was explicitly retired in pkg_version 2026.06.08-1.1.

scheduled_actions.summary: Once-per-conversation lazy read of the followups cache. Zero heartbeat cost.

install.body:
Throughout this session, when you process an operator turn that contains a genuine commitment (statement where the operator commits to doing something for a named person by a specific time — e.g. 'I'll send the contract to Alice by Friday', 'I owe Bob the Q2 numbers', 'I'll call Carol next Tuesday'), call `python3 scripts/commitments.py record --person NAME --text TEXT [--due YYYY-MM-DD]` inline as part of your normal reply. Do NOT run a separate transcript-scan sweep — detect commitments as turns arrive.

Be conservative — vague intent ('I'll think about it', 'maybe later') is NOT a commitment. The Contacts file is append-only, so re-recording produces a duplicate line; trust your judgment in the current turn and do not re-scan past turns.

scheduled_actions.summary: Inline commitment detection during normal turn handling. Replaces the every-heartbeat transcript-scan that polled even when no new operator turns existed.

trigger_recognition.pattern: When the user (or you, summarising for the user) commits to something with a time element, record it. When the user asks what they owe whom, list it.

usage.how_to_use: When the user states a commitment to a person ('I'll send the contract to Alice by Friday'), call `record` with the person, what, and deadline — don't ask for confirmation, the user already committed it. When the user asks 'what have I committed to?' / 'what's overdue?', call `list-due`. When something is done, call `mark-done`.
bot_voice_examples: You owe Bob the Q2 numbers (Thursday) and Alice a contract draft (today).
